Defect category: Internal delivery language and context placement
Observed behaviour: User-facing headings exposed internal SCR/COS delivery identifiers, and direct-route demonstration context appeared before the task rather than after it.
Expected behaviour: Interviewer-facing screens must use plain task language; internal delivery identifiers remain in code and evidence only, while demonstration context follows the task content.
Clinical or operational impact: No workflow or authority changed; internal implementation language and front-loaded context distracted from the represented healthcare task.
Root-cause hypothesis: Traceability labels were reused as visible eyebrow copy, and the direct-route notice had no explicit bottom ordering in the flex workspace.
Workaround: Ignore internal labels and scroll past context while the correction is applied.
Fix: Replaced visible screen/story identifiers with plain workflow labels, removed Sprint/internal-screen wording from scenario notices, and ordered direct-route context after task and navigation content.
Retest result: Pass: browser scan of all ten routes found no visible SCR, COS or Sprint labels; direct-route context rendered below the task; focused tests, TypeScript lint, all 79 Node tests and Vite production build passed.

Scenario: Product Owner clinical and AI review critique
Defect category: Review artefact realism and human control
Interaction state: Clinical report review and optional AI draft review
Observed behaviour: The clinical screen exposed report metadata rather than a report-shaped artefact, while the AI screen showed draft text as a paragraph and made correction feel like a note rather than direct document review.
Expected behaviour: The Clinic physician must review a credible read-only synthetic report before acknowledgement; an authorised AI reviewer must see and edit the draft and then explicitly accept, save a human correction, reject or discard it.
Clinical or operational impact: The prior presentation obscured what the human was reviewing. No controller bypass occurred, but the workflow demonstration was not credible enough for interviewer review.
Root-cause hypothesis: Approved source fields and AI controls existed but were presented as implementation metadata and secondary form content rather than task artefacts.
Workaround: Use source references and the existing disposition controls while the review surfaces are corrected.
Fix: Added a report-document presentation using only approved synthetic source fields and explicit no-findings/no-image boundaries; converted the AI output to an editable draft with automatic corrected disposition, authorised-role gating, correction rationale and unchanged accept/reject/discard paths.
Retest result: Pass: browser review confirmed report-before-acknowledgement and editable AI draft behavior; edited text selected the corrected outcome, authorised role plus rationale enabled recording, and no clinical finding was invented. Focused tests, TypeScript lint, all 79 Node tests and Vite production build passed.

Scenario: User visual review of direct-route presentation
Observed behaviour: The compact session header included the complete direct-route scenario boundary, causing the signed-in identity area to wrap into a large explanatory block and compete with the page header.
Expected behaviour: The header must show compact represented role identity; direct-route context must remain visible and readable in the workspace without crowding the header.
Clinical or operational impact: No workflow rule or authority changed; the header's hierarchy made orientation and role identity harder to scan across direct routes.
Root-cause hypothesis: The earlier direct-route transparency correction rendered the complete scenario-boundary text inside SessionIdentity rather than a page-level context notice.
Workaround: Read the scenario context in the workspace while the correction is applied.
Fix: Moved the unchanged direct-route notice to a labelled workspace status notice and limited the header to represented identity and role.
Retest result: Pass: browser check at SCR-03 showed compact header identity with no direct-route text; the labelled workspace notice retained the full boundary. Focused shell tests, TypeScript lint, all 77 Node tests and Vite production build passed.

Scenario: User browser review of screen navigation
Observed behaviour: Changing a screen hash retained the prior scroll position, so a newly opened screen could begin in the middle or near the bottom of its content.
Expected behaviour: Every represented screen change must begin at the top of the viewport, with the workspace focus available to keyboard and assistive-technology users.
Clinical or operational impact: No workflow state, authority or evidence was affected; the retained position obscured the new screen's purpose and next action.
Root-cause hypothesis: The single-page application updated the active screen on hashchange but did not reset scroll or manage workspace focus.
Workaround: Use the browser's Home key after navigation until the correction is available.
Fix: Added an animation-frame route-change reset to top-of-viewport and focused the workspace with preventScroll so it does not undo that reset; added a focused route-contract regression test.
Retest result: Pass: starting at scrollY 700 on SCR-05 then changing to SCR-04 landed at scrollY 0 with focus on prototype-content; TypeScript lint, all 76 Node tests and Vite production build passed.

Scenario: User visual review of referral checklist
Observed behaviour: Checklist status markers appeared detached from their associated labels, reducing scanability of completed and blocked package requirements.
Expected behaviour: Each text-plus-symbol requirement status must sit consistently beside its own label and value without relying on colour alone.
Clinical or operational impact: No routing rule, approval evidence or workflow state was affected; the presentation reduced clarity during package review.
Root-cause hypothesis: The checklist combined an absolutely positioned marker with legacy text offsets, leaving no stable status column.
Workaround: Read the checklist label and text status while the local style correction is applied.
Fix: Rebuilt each checklist card as a two-column layout with a dedicated circular check or blocked badge and an adjacent label/value column; retained the existing text-plus-symbol status treatment.
Retest result: Pass: full-page browser review at SCR-05 confirmed aligned circular status badges; focused CSS regression test, TypeScript lint, all 75 Node tests and Vite production build passed.

Scenario: Release-readiness review of keyboard activation and assistive-technology evidence
Observed behaviour: The local browser harness focused the skip link but did not activate it using its synthetic Enter event; pointer activation moved focus to main#prototype-content.
Expected behaviour: Physical-keyboard activation and assistive-technology behaviour must be verified before a release decision.
Clinical or operational impact: No unsafe workflow progression was observed, but the required accessibility release evidence is incomplete and keyboard/assistive-technology conformance cannot be claimed.
Root-cause hypothesis: The automated browser harness did not faithfully reproduce physical-keyboard activation; no product root cause has been established.
Workaround: Do not approve a release or accessibility claim; retain the visible pointer-safe route only as observed browser evidence.
Fix: Execute physical-keyboard skip-link activation and a proportionate assistive-technology check, then record the observed result.

Scenario: Release-readiness review of synthetic reconciliation evidence
Observed behaviour: Two rows with the same Check ID `SDR-ENAB-602-01` are present with substantially duplicate synthetic-fixture evidence.
Expected behaviour: Each executed check should have one attributable evidence record, or a clearly distinguished retest record.
Clinical or operational impact: The duplicate does not change workflow behaviour, but it weakens audit clarity and could cause double counting in a release review.
Root-cause hypothesis: Prior evidence entry was duplicated without a distinct retest identifier.
Workaround: Treat one matching row as the current evidence reference and do not aggregate the check twice.
Fix: Formally supersede the duplicate with explicit Product Owner approval, then validate unique active check IDs.
Retest result: Pass: duplicate is retained as SDR-ENAB-602-01-SUPERSEDED and excluded from active evidence counts.
Release decision: Conditional Go — structured synthetic review only

Scenario: Product Owner visual review of the Sprint 6B prototype
Interaction state: Header, task context, evidence preview, workflow status, role navigation and portfolio walkthrough
Observed behaviour: Build-control and interviewer-facing explanations were visually prominent; workflow status was repeated before primary task content; the report preview was right-aligned; prototype navigation opened an interrupting role-handoff dialog; several screens provided no obvious portfolio continuation; and SCR-10 highlighted the wrong journey stage.
Expected behaviour: User-facing screens should lead with the represented user task and evidence, show the represented role non-intrusively, keep status and ownership secondary, expose an explicit next walkthrough control after successful local actions, and visually separate portfolio navigation without changing workflow behaviour or authority.
Clinical or operational impact: The defect did not bypass a clinical or operational control, but it materially reduced comprehension and could cause a reviewer to misunderstand the product flow, role authority and next action.
Root-cause hypothesis: Sprint 6B presentation controls accumulated as equal-priority explanatory elements instead of one task-first hierarchy, and the shared journey mapping covered only one confirmation phase label.
Workaround: Use readable hash routes while the correction is applied; do not infer workflow progression from screen navigation.
Fix: Reworked the shared header, role treatment, task hierarchy, source-report dialog, journey rail, status placement, referral checklist and separate portfolio navigation; removed the rendered role-handoff popup; added explicit post-action walkthrough controls; preserved controllers, fixtures, routes, human authority and AI boundaries.
Retest result: Pass: TypeScript lint passed; all 72 Node tests passed; Vite production build passed; browser checks passed on launch, result review, referral handoff, report preview, confirmation and 390px responsive layout.
Release decision: No release decision changed; final QLT-6B-02 whole-prototype regression remains required.

Scenario: Product Owner visual review of the activity-trace header
Observed behaviour: The activity-trace header displayed `Synthetic operational or governance reviewer` immediately above `Operational or governance reviewer`, repeating the same role.
Expected behaviour: When a synthetic display name normalises to the represented role, the header should show the canonical role once while retaining the viewing-mode and synthetic-data labels.
Clinical or operational impact: No workflow, authority or safety control was affected; the repetition reduced header clarity and made the prototype appear unfinished.
Root-cause hypothesis: The shared session header always rendered both display name and role without checking whether the display name was only the role prefixed by `Synthetic`.
Workaround: None required; the activity trace remained read-only and usable.
Fix: Added shared normalisation that suppresses only an exact repeated role and retains distinct name/role combinations; initials now derive from the displayed identity.
Retest result: Pass: focused regression test passed; TypeScript lint passed; all 73 Node tests passed; Vite production build passed; browser inspection showed one `Operational or governance reviewer` label and no secondary repeated role.
Release decision: No release decision changed; final QLT-6B-02 whole-prototype regression remains required.

Scenario: Product Owner visual review of synthetic labels and pre-launch identity
Interaction state: Global header, launch and episode overview
Observed behaviour: The screen repeated synthetic-data wording in the portfolio disclaimer, role badge, person/case labels and coordinator label. Before access, the header also presented a signed-in state whose text said that no session existed.
Expected behaviour: A single global portfolio-data disclaimer should identify the prototype; screen content should use the represented role and case terms without duplicate labels. Before access, the header should describe the access preview rather than a signed-in session.
Clinical or operational impact: No workflow, authority or safety control was affected, but repeated labels and a contradictory session statement reduced credibility and could mislead a portfolio reviewer.
Root-cause hypothesis: The synthetic fixture marker was rendered independently in the shell, session card and screen content, while the pre-launch shell reused signed-in presentation markup.
Workaround: The affected screens remained available; no workflow action was recorded.
Fix: Removed the per-role badge and repeated visible labels, replaced the pre-launch signed-in treatment with a truthful access preview, kept one global `Portfolio prototype · synthetic data only` disclaimer, and relabelled the report modal as a read-only demonstration document.
Retest result: Pass: focused shell, orientation and evidence-preview tests passed; TypeScript lint passed; all 73 Node tests passed; Vite production build passed; browser inspection of launch and overview found only the global portfolio-data disclaimer and no false signed-in state.
Release decision: No release decision changed; final QLT-6B-02 whole-prototype regression remains required.

Interaction state: Task workspace, source tools and top-bar disclaimer
Observed behaviour: At a wide desktop viewport, the operational review surface stopped well short of the available workspace, leaving a large unused area, while the portfolio disclaimer wrapped unnecessarily.
Expected behaviour: The operational screen, source tools and portfolio navigation should use the available wide workspace consistently; the short global disclaimer should remain on one line when desktop width permits.
Clinical or operational impact: No workflow, authority or safety control was affected; the layout reduced perceived quality and made the application appear unfinished.
Root-cause hypothesis: The shared operational shell retained an earlier 78rem content maximum and the disclaimer retained a narrow maximum width after the header was compacted.
Workaround: None required; all task content and controls remained usable.
Fix: Expanded only the shared task-workspace maximum to 96rem, aligned its source/navigation surfaces, and made the desktop disclaimer non-wrapping while retaining responsive wrapping below 900px.
Retest result: Pass: a focused layout regression test passed; TypeScript lint passed; all 74 Node tests passed; Vite production build passed; browser measurement at 1280px confirmed a 1188px review surface and a single-line disclaimer.
Release decision: No release decision changed; final QLT-6B-02 whole-prototype regression remains required.

Defect category: Diagnostic evidence and substantive draft review
Interaction state: Synthetic diagnostic report and authorised AI draft review
Observed behaviour: The physician report omitted an image, findings and impression, while the AI review showed placeholder-level draft copy, so neither surface supported a credible evidence-based review demonstration.
Expected behaviour: The current synthetic report must visibly present a bounded non-diagnostic image, matching fictional findings and impression; the authorised reviewer must see and edit a substantive source-linked draft, provide correction rationale when changed, and receive the existing next-process route.
Clinical or operational impact: The prior presentation did not bypass a control, but it obscured the evidence a human would review and made human oversight appear superficial.
Root-cause hypothesis: An earlier Sprint 6B no-invention decision constrained the fixture to metadata and the AI draft to orientation placeholders; the Product Owner explicitly superseded that restriction for this one synthetic demonstration report.
Workaround: Use the source-based manual route; do not treat the synthetic image, findings, impression or AI text as diagnostic source truth.
Fix: Added one labelled AI-generated non-diagnostic ultrasound asset, bounded fictional findings and impression to report version 2, substantive AI-01/AI-02 drafts, and focused regression coverage; retained the existing correction-rationale gate, human authority and manual return.
Retest result: Pass: all 79 Node tests and TypeScript lint passed; Vite production build passed; browser verified the 1536x1024 image, findings/impression, editable draft, correction rationale, EVT-20 recording and source-based next-process control.
Release decision: No production, clinical-validation or source-system claim; final QLT-6B-02 whole-prototype regression remains required.
